cargo.chosen: (c) tool-native — `[workspace.package] license-file = "LICENSE"` + `license-file.workspace = true` on each of the 7 publishable crates.
cargo.measurement: An INHERITED license-file resolves relative to the WORKSPACE ROOT (not the crate dir). `cargo package --list -p fathomdb-query` listed `LICENSE`; `cargo package --no-verify` produced a tarball whose fathomdb-query-0.8.9/LICENSE is 1078 bytes, sha256-identical to the repo root, and whose packaged Cargo.toml was rewritten to `license-file = "LICENSE"`. Repeated for all 7 (6 byte-proven, engine --list-proven; see BLK-1). cargo 1.95.0. No warning emitted for carrying both `license` and `license-file`.
alternatives_measured_and_rejected: (b) symlink per crate: MEASURED WORKING — `src/rust/crates/fathomdb-schema/LICENSE -> ../../../../LICENSE` was dereferenced into the .crate with real 1078-byte content. Rejected anyway: a git checkout without symlink support materialises it as a text stub containing the path, which would publish a LICENSE file whose content is the string `../../../../LICENSE`. The chosen mechanism has no such failure mode.
(a) a real copy in each of the 7 crate dirs: works, but 7 duplicates that can drift, for zero benefit over (c).

A literal (non-inherited) `license-file = "../../../../LICENSE"` on one crate ALSO worked (listed and packaged as `LICENSE`). CORRECTION TO THE DESIGN/BRIEF: the constraint that `cargo package` refuses paths outside the package root is true of `include`, but NOT of `license-file` — cargo copies a license-file in from outside the root. Rejected only because the inherited form is one line in the workspace instead of a different `../../../../` string per crate.

npm.chosen: A REAL COPY of LICENSE in each npm package dir (src/ts, src/ts/npm/linux-x64-gnu).
npm.measurement: npm's automatic license inclusion DOES beat the `files: ["dist"]` allowlist — but only for a regular file. A symlink `src/ts/LICENSE -> ../../LICENSE` produced a tarball with NO license entry at all (`tar -tzf` -> `package/LICENSE: Not found in archive`; total files unchanged at 13). Replacing it with a real copy: 14 files, `npm notice 1.1kB LICENSE`, tarball content sha256-identical to root. This is why the guard REQUIRES a regular file and rejects a symlink with a message naming the measurement.
npm.drift_mitigation: The guard asserts byte-equality of every copy against the root LICENSE (test arm 10 proves that assertion fires).

python.chosen: PEP-639 `license = "MIT"` + `license-files = ["LICENSE"]`, with a real copy at src/python/LICENSE.
python.measurement: Verified BY BUILDING, per the brief. `maturin build` with maturin 1.13.1 -> Metadata-Version 2.4, License-Expression: MIT, License-File: LICENSE, and .dist-info/licenses/LICENSE byte-identical. PEP 639 forbids `..` in license-files globs, so a copy is unavoidable here (the guard asserts byte-equality and test arm 7 proves the `..` rejection fires).

blockers_encountered.resolution: NOT MINE TO FIX and not a license defect. Verified PRE-EXISTING: reproduced identically after `git stash` to the pristine baseline 3e9d6d12. FOR SLICE 40: this is a live dependency of the T5 engine publish on T4 having landed first; worth an explicit check in the dry-run rehearsal.

blockers_encountered.description: The pinned build backend `maturin>=1.7,<2` cannot build the chosen PEP-639 license form. Measured, not reasoned: `maturin sdist` exits 1 on 1.7.8 AND on 1.8.0 with `TOML parse error ... license-files = ["LICENSE"] wanted string or table` (both predate final PEP 639, which changed license-files from a table to a list of globs), and exits 0 on 1.9.0 / 1.10.0 / 1.11.0 / 1.12.0 / 1.13.1.
blockers_encountered.resolution: Raised the floor to `maturin>=1.9,<2` in src/python/pyproject.toml — build-system requires AND the two extras that install maturin for `maturin develop`. This is a build-backend requirement, NOT a project version field, so it does not touch Slice 40's bump. The alternative (keeping the legacy `license = { text = ... }` table) was rejected: it produces no License-Expression and does not ship license text. FOR SLICE 40: confirm PyO3/maturin-action@v1.51.0 resolves maturin >= 1.9 (it installs latest by default, so almost certainly yes, but it is one line in the dry run).
